possibleUses: In gameplay, Quest Chain Compounding can support linked objective bonuses, escalating reward ladders, and route-planning incentives across quest hubs or campaigns. It makes structure itself a source of power. That is useful for players who like planning and momentum rather than isolated tasks. It also creates a clean way to reward engagement with the quest graph.

In narrative and quests, it enables pressure-cooker mission chains, rival interruption arcs, and stories about whether optimization is eroding compassion. The bearer can save a region through perfect sequencing or fail morally by treating people like nodes in a combo route. That tension gives the Framework real dramatic bite. It also helps the narrator explain why some characters always seem one step ahead.

In implementation, it fits chain metadata, reward multipliers, dependency graphs, momentum counters, and branching-quest continuity tracking. Those hooks can enrich the quest manager without forcing a rewrite of every quest definition. They also pair well with narrator summaries and system messaging. That makes the Framework highly practical.

Its limitation-aware use comes from making every chain valuable but narrowing, because the best reward route is not always the best moral or strategic route. The player should occasionally want to break a profitable chain for a human reason. That preserves agency and tone. The strongest version rewards coherence without punishing conscience out of existence.
limits: Compounding only works across genuinely related objectives, so random disconnected task spam should not build serious momentum.
The Framework is vulnerable to interruption, branching chaos, and urgent crises that force the bearer off the ideal route.
Overcommitting to one chain can leave the player unprepared for unrelated threats or social damage outside the optimized path.
costs: Maintaining chain momentum pressures the bearer to prioritize sequence efficiency even when people need help outside the reward route.
Breaking a profitable chain can feel materially painful, which creates real temptation to become callous or compulsively optimization-driven.
High-value chains attract sabotage from rivals who understand that disrupting continuity may matter more than winning a fair fight.
worldCompatibility: Quest Chain Compounding organizes existing objective structure and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the deeper laws that define worthy causality.
It is compatible with quest graphs, faction campaigns, divine errands, and progression pacing because it structures continuity rather than brute force.
Its strongest rewards still require real quests, real continuity, and real risk, which keeps the Framework subtle but balanced.

name: Reality Edit Interface
summary: A causality-editing Framework that applies bounded local parameter changes and forces the bearer to live with the consequences.
description: Reality Edit Interface is a Framework that exposes a narrow operational layer for editing small local properties of objects, spaces, and interactions. It belongs in the Framework category because it provides a bounded interface and accounting model for changes rather than granting limitless authorship over reality. The bearer can identify editable parameters such as friction, brittleness, pressure, balance, or symbolic state and then spend causality charge to nudge them out of normal alignment. Its progression bias favors precision, preparation, and indirect problem solving instead of overwhelming frontal force. Small edits can produce dramatic outcomes, but only when the bearer understands context well enough to exploit the cascade they are about to start. The main tradeoff is causality stress, because reality resists repeated tampering and begins to charge interest in the form of paradox residue, correction events, and hostile attention. In the world, Reality Edit Interface should feel uncanny and deeply alarming because ordinary witnesses see impossible coincidences while experts realize someone is touching the hidden sliders beneath the surface. It remains lore-safe because edits stay local, expensive, and vulnerable to stronger law, anti-edit fields, or simply the bearer misreading which variable actually matters.
coreLoop: Identify a local parameter that the interface can lawfully expose and decide whether changing it is worth the causality charge.
Apply the edit inside a bounded scope and immediately adapt to the chain reaction it creates in the environment, object, or encounter.
Manage residue, correction pressure, and enemy scrutiny before repeated edits turn a clever exploit into a catastrophic paradox.
progression: Early growth increases causality charge, improves parameter visibility, and allows safe manipulation of physical properties in a tightly bounded area.
Mid progression unlocks chained edits, environment-level tuning, and carefully limited conceptual adjustments such as fear, luck, or symbolic weight.
Late progression turns the bearer into a terrifying tactician who can unravel stronger foes by touching a few decisive variables at exactly the wrong moment.
narrativeHooks: You can engineer disasters that look like coincidence until too many impossible outcomes point back to your hand.
Guardians of time, law, and ritual order hunt you because every edit suggests the world is more editable than they want anyone to know.
The Framework steadily tempts the bearer to treat people and places as parameter sets instead of as lives and histories.
questHooks: Collapse an enemy fortress by finding the one structural or symbolic parameter whose failure will cascade through the whole defense network.
Save a city by editing the wrongness out of a ritual accident before the causality debt rolls forward into mass catastrophe.
Steal a forbidden grammar of edits from a guardian archive that insists no mortal should ever see the world rendered as variables.
possibleUses: In gameplay, Reality Edit Interface can support environmental manipulation, trap setup, object sabotage, temporary property edits, and carefully scoped conceptual debuffs. It rewards players who notice leverage points instead of only chasing bigger numbers. That creates a powerful tactical identity across combat, stealth, and puzzle play. It also makes knowledge of the scene matter more than raw stats alone.

In narrative and quests, it enables improbable assassinations, miracle-like rescues, ritual corrections, and eerie scenes where one tiny change topples a much larger structure. The bearer can defeat stronger enemies by understanding what is fragile in them or around them. They can also catastrophically overreach if they treat every problem as a variable to be forced. That tension gives the Framework sharp dramatic teeth.

In implementation, it maps well to tagged properties, scoped edit actions, causality charge, deferred backlash, and correction-event hooks layered on existing systems. Those pieces can feed encounter scripting, object interactions, prompt context, and risk messaging without requiring a universal simulation rewrite. It also gives designers a clear place to store what can and cannot be edited on key content. That makes the Framework implementable even though its fantasy sounds broad.

Its limitation-aware use comes from keeping edits local, interpretable, and costly. The player should feel clever because they found the right seam, not because they can rewrite anything they dislike. Strong use should look like technical causality abuse under pressure. That preserves the category line between bounded interface and godlike reality authorship.
limits: Only bounded local parameters can be edited directly, and many protected, sacred, or sovereign properties are outside the interface entirely.
The bearer must correctly identify what variable matters, because a clever but mistaken edit can waste charge or trigger a worse cascade.
Repeated edits in the same scene increase correction pressure and make future changes less stable and more dangerous.
costs: Every edit consumes causality charge and leaves residue that can surface later as backlash, paradox, or hostile scrutiny.
Broad or concept-level edits are especially expensive and can harm allies, bystanders, or the environment if the cascade is misjudged.
Using the interface too often encourages a detached mindset that treats reality as an editable board rather than a lived world.
worldCompatibility: Reality Edit Interface manipulates local parameters inside existing law and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the highest structures that define reality itself.
It is compatible with traps, rituals, puzzles, environmental combat, and narrator consequence systems because it routes edits through scoped variables and explicit cost.
Its strongest effects require context mastery, bounded targets, and acceptance of correction risk, which keeps the Framework potent without becoming unrestricted authorship.

name: Dungeon Core Mastery (Living Dungeon System)
summary: A living-dungeon Framework that binds the bearer to a core and turns territorial growth into rooms, monsters, traps, and layered infrastructure.
description: Dungeon Core Mastery is a Framework that fuses the bearer with a dungeon core or an equivalent living control nexus. It belongs in the Framework category because it organizes territorial growth, room logic, spawning, and dungeon infrastructure instead of functioning as a free-floating System usable anywhere. The bearer becomes responsible for shaping an enclosed ecosystem of danger, reward, mana flow, and defensive design. Its progression bias favors territory building, trap architecture, resource routing, and monster curation rather than portable personal supremacy. The dungeon grows as an organism and institution, meaning advancement is measured in complexity, throughput, survivability, and the quality of what the core can sustain. The main tradeoff is immobility and exposure, because the heart of the Framework is tied to a site that enemies can invade, corrupt, starve, or besiege. In the world, Dungeon Core Mastery should be treated as both an economic engine and a strategic threat because a mature living dungeon can shape migration, wealth, frontier survival, and regional war. It remains lore-safe because the Framework is powerful only through managed territory, mana intake, infrastructure, and defendable growth, not through unrestricted authority over the wider world.
coreLoop: Shape rooms, routes, traps, monster ecology, and reward flow so the dungeon grows stronger when intruders engage with it.
Convert mana, harvested resources, and invasion outcomes into structural upgrades, new sectors, and improved core functions.
Defend the heart of the dungeon while deciding whether the territory will become a proving ground, a refuge, a factory, or a predatory maze.
progression: Early growth grants simple room templates, low-tier monster spawning, basic trap logic, and enough control to keep the core alive.
Mid progression expands into multi-floor specialization, elite encounters, environmental themes, and internal production or crafting sectors.
Late progression turns the dungeon into a living polity whose economy, defenses, and reputation can influence an entire region.
narrativeHooks: People who enter your domain are forced to decide whether they are raiders, pilgrims, workers, or prey, and your layout answers that question for them.
The dungeon slowly becomes a mirror of the bearer's values, whether that means disciplined trial, ecological weirdness, ruthless extraction, or shelter behind teeth.
Every expansion raises the same uncomfortable question: are you building a home, a weapon, or a machine that has already outgrown your right to guide it?
questHooks: Secure a stabilizing heart-material before your core fractures under the stress of recent expansion.
Defeat or absorb a rival living dungeon whose growth model is poisoning the frontier around both your territories.
Use the dungeon itself to shelter a region through disaster while deciding how much danger outsiders must survive to earn that safety.
possibleUses: In gameplay, Dungeon Core Mastery can support room building, trap placement, monster spawning, invasion routing, and territory-based progression loops. It gives dungeon play a true growth framework instead of treating a dungeon as just a combat backdrop. That is useful for strategy-minded players who want to build layered defenses and economies. It also creates strong asymmetry between home-territory power and expedition vulnerability.

In narrative and quests, it enables frontier survival arcs, rival-core wars, settlement dependence, and moral choices about how a living dungeon should treat those who enter it. The bearer can become a local guardian, tyrant, provider, or catastrophe. That flexibility makes the Framework story-rich without losing coherence. It also naturally supports long regional plots because a dungeon changes everything around it.

In implementation, it fits dungeon-state graphs, room templates, encounter tables, mana-income loops, core integrity, and territory upgrades. Those hooks already align with multiple parts of the repo, including quests, rewards, generation, faction response, and narrator summaries. It also pairs well with crafting and summoning without needing to subsume them. That makes it one of the most integration-friendly infrastructure frameworks available.

Its limitation-aware use comes from tying nearly all of its greatness to place. Away from the dungeon, the bearer should retain insight, prepared assets, and partial support, but not the full oppressive advantage of the core itself. That contrast keeps the fantasy strategic instead of all-purpose. The strongest version feels like being the heart of a dangerous ecosystem, not carrying an infinite portable fortress in your pocket.
limits: The Framework is anchored to a real core site, so its strongest powers cannot be projected indefinitely beyond the managed dungeon territory.
Growth depends on mana flow, materials, invasion pressure, and the ability to protect core infrastructure from siege, corruption, or theft.
A poorly designed dungeon can become unstable, economically useless, politically targeted, or internally hostile to its own purpose.
costs: Maintaining a living dungeon consumes constant resources, planning time, and defense effort even when no immediate crisis is visible.
Every expansion makes the bearer more strategically valuable and therefore more likely to attract guild assault, state intervention, or rival-core predation.
The moral cost can be severe, because the dungeon must decide how much suffering, risk, and exploitation it is willing to build into its own growth loop.
worldCompatibility: Dungeon Core Mastery organizes territorial growth inside existing world law and cannot surpass Void, Grandmother Void, or the higher structures that authorize reality.
It is compatible with dungeon simulation, settlement pressure, encounter generation, and regional politics because it structures a bounded growth engine.
Its power remains grounded in place, infrastructure, upkeep, and siege vulnerability, which keeps the Framework massive in influence but clearly bounded.
